The proposed changes come as Korea reassesses its international student policy amid growing concerns that aggressive recruitment by universities — sometimes involving inducement of guaranteeing part-time work — may come at the expense of educational quality. The number of international students in Korea stood at 307,464 as of April, surpassing the government's 2027 target of 300,000 ahead of schedule. The figure rises to nearly 400,000 when including some 30,000 graduates seeking employment. Kim Tae-kyu said in a press release. The PPP claimed that Cho's team had violated a law criminalizing the distortion of law that took effect in March. "This year's Suneung was an unfamiliar experience for both students and teachers," Han said on X. "As teachers checked the students' glasses and clothing, they likely remained on edge until the very end, anxious about whether anything had been overlooked, yet equally concerned that an unnecessary suspicion might hurt a student's feelings." Rep. Lee Ju-hee and 18 DPK colleagues have submitted an amendment to the Information and Communications Network Act to require makers and importers of wearable cameras to include a recording indicator that people nearby can easily recognize. It is one of two bills in what the lawmaker calls the “Smart Glasses Illegal Filming Prevention Act,” introduced earlier this week. The other bill would also require individuals who film others with such devices to signal that they are recording. Existing rules cover only the stage when footage is distributed, according to the lawmakers. items.summary: The Constitutional Court ruled Thursday that a provision of the Immigration Act imposing a general ban on political activity by foreign residents does not conform to the Constitution, with six of the nine judges agreeing. To prevent a legal vacuum, however, the court kept the clause in effect until it can be revised, no later than Dec. 31, 2028. The provision was introduced in 1977. A 2005 amendment added an exception for political activities permitted under other laws, but the general ban stayed in place. Violators can be ordered to halt the activity or leave the country and those without permanent resident status may face deportation. In 2021, two Mongolian international students planned to reques preliminary candidates in the 20th presidential election present policies to address discrimination against foreign nationals living in Korea. items.title: Saudi transport and logistics investments set to hit SR45 billion in 2026
items.title_zh: 沙特运输和物流投资预计在2026年将达到450亿里亚尔
items.summary: RIYADH — Minister of Transport and Logistics Saleh Al-Jasser said Saudi Arabia’s transport and logistics sector has made significant progress, surpassing several Saudi Vision 2030 targets ahead of schedule. He said that new investment commitments in the sector are expected to reach SR45 billion in 2026, despite regional challenges.Speaking at a panel discussion titled "Logistical and technical capabilities connecting the world" at the Budget 2027 Forum in Riyadh on Wednesday, Al-Jasser said the transport and logistics sector operates as an integrated system encompassing regulatory and legislative entities across civil aviation, transport, roads, and ports, working in closecoordination with the private sector.He described the private sector as the main driver of investment and resources underpinning the National Transport and Logistics Strategy, noting that the Kingdom has attracted hundreds of billions of riyals in high-quality investments from major international companies in recent years.He cited Maersk's investment at Jeddah Islamic Port, which hosts the company's largest logistics zone worldwide. The facility has reached full occupancy, prompting the company to seek further investment opportunities in the Kingdom.Jeddah Islamic Port currently has 17 integrated logistics zones. Al-Jasser also noted that multibillion-riyal investment agreements were signed this year with CMA CGM to develop a terminal at the port, alongside contracts for five new logistics zones. In the railway sector, he highlighted the procurement of 20 new trainsets for the Haramain High-Speed Railway, in addition to new rolling stock for the Eastern, Northern, and mining railway lines.He added that contracts had been signed to double-track the mining railway line, which supports the transportation of three types of minerals, while the project to connect the Kingdom's railway networks through a link in Riyadh had reached its final tendering stage. Efforts are also underway to complete the Landbridge project in partnership with the private sector.Al-Jasser said women's participation in the sector had risen to 33 percent of the workforce, while the Saudization rate in leadership and highly skilled positions had reached approximately two-thirds. He attributed this progress to the establishment of specialized academies offering internationally recognized training programs closely linked to private-sector employment needs. The minister also highlighted technological advances that have transformed jobs such as operating large port cranes and driving modern trains, including those on the Haramain High-Speed Railway and Al Mashaaer Al Mugaddassah Metro, into advanced career opportunities for Saudi men and women. Al-Jasser acknowledged the continued support of the Kingdom's leadership for the transport and logistics sector, stressing that it remains committed to balancing flexible and rapid responses to exceptional challenges with the continuity of daily operations and the efficient implementation of major strategic and transformative projects.

items.summary: RIYADH — The Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced on Wednesday that S&P Global Ratings has assigned its inaugural A+ long-term foreign and local currency issuer credit ratings, with a stable outlook. PIF’s existing A-1 short-term rating remains unchanged, with PIF’s ratings in line with those of Saudi Arabia.The A+ rating reflects confidence in PIF’s long-term strategy and its strong financial position. It further adds to PIF’s already strong credit profile, thereby supporting its sustainable funding base and long-term investment strategy.S&P’s assessment highlighted PIF’s diversified funding profile, moderate leverage position and its focus on value realization under PIF’s 2026-2030 strategy, as well as its critical role in driving Saudi Arabia’s economic transformation.PIF’s Head of Capital Finance Strategy Ziyad Alfawzan said: “The inaugural A+ long-term rating from S&P marks an important milestone in the continued development of PIF’s credit profile and our long-term funding plan. PIF holds strong long-term credit ratings from S&P, Moody’s and Fitch, reflecting PIF’s diversified and sustainable funding base and the strength of its financial profile and governance. It further reflects confidence in PIF’s long-term strategy, as we advance the 2026-2030 value realization phase.”The S&P rating adds to PIF’s robust credit profile. Moody’s Ratings confirmed PIF’s aa3 baseline credit assessment and Aa3 long-term issuer rating with a stable outlook remain unchanged following a periodic review, in September. Fitch Ratings also affirmed PIF’s long-term foreign and local currency issuer default ratings at 'A+' with a stable outlook, in October.PIF holds strong ratings from each of the world’s three leading credit rating agencies:* S&P: Long-term A+ and short-term A-1 (stable outlook)* Moody’s: Long-term Aa3, short-term P-1 (stable outlook)* Fitch: Long-term A+, short-term F1+ (stable outlook)PIF is one of the world’s most impactful investors, with a long-term investment strategy to further drive the economic transformation of Saudi Arabia and deliver sustainable financial returns.

items.title: Houthi projectile hits Jazan port, no injuries reported
items.title_zh: 胡塞武装的炮弹击中吉赞港，未有人员受伤的报告
items.summary: RIYADH — A projectile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia fell at Jazan port, causing minor damage but no civilian casualties. Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, stated that efforts were underway to determine the type of projectile used.

items.title: Al-Mushaiti: Private-sector investments in agriculture sector surpass SR60 billion
items.title_zh: Al-Mushaiti：私营部门对农业领域的投资超过600亿里亚尔
items.summary: RIYADH — Deputy Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture Eng. Mansour Al-Mushaiti said that the agricultural sector is a key pillar of food security and a driver of economic and social development. “Over the past 10 years, the Agricultural Development Fund has provided loans exceeding SR40 billion, equivalent to the total amount it had extended over the preceding five decades. This has helped stimulate private-sector investment in agriculture, which has exceeded SR60 billion,” he said while attending the Budget 2027 Forum in Riyadh on Wednesday.Al-Mushaiti said that these investments had contributed to increasing agricultural production from 6 million tons in 2015 to more than 13 million tons in 2025, while the sector's contribution to gross domestic product (GDP) rose from SR54 billion to SR124 billion over the same period. The deputy minister emphasized that Saudi Arabia is now reaping the rewards of a decade of achievements under Saudi Vision 2030. “The Kingdom continues to pursue its targets through a development model that measures progress by tangible results and the economic and social benefits experienced by citizens,” he said. Al-Mushaiti noted that the environment, water, and agriculture system had achieved significant milestones in food security, water security, and environmental sustainability, with generous support from the wise leadership. The deputy minister reviewed the key achievements of the environment, water, and agriculture sectors. He highlighted the impact of government investments and partnerships with the private sector in promoting sustainable development, improving resource efficiency, and achieving national targets. Al-Mushaiti also noted that the Sustainable Agricultural Rural Development Program (Saudi Reef) represents an effective model for translating government support into lasting economic and social benefits. Over seven years, the government invested SR3 billion in the program, generating economic returns of SR10.7 billion, providing more than 92,000 income-generating opportunities, and increasing rural production by more than 480,000 tons, in line with the comparative advantages of different regions. Al-Mushaiti stressed that Saudi Arabia had adopted a balanced approach to agricultural development, combining increased production and stronger food security with the preservation of natural resources. This has resulted in a reduction of more than 40 percent in non-renewable groundwater consumption, from 21 billion cubic meters to less than 11 billion cubic meters. On environmental sustainability, he said the Kingdom was leading a green era through local, regional, and international initiatives, driven by its belief that environmental sustainability is a gateway to development and prosperity. These initiatives reflect the Kingdom's commitment to protecting the environment and promoting the sustainability of resources at regional and global levels. He reviewed key achievements of the Saudi Green Initiative, which has helped increase the proportion of protected areas from 4 percent in 2015 to more than 18 percent of the Kingdom's total area, with a target of reaching 30 percent by 2030. The initiative has also contributed to the rehabilitation of 1.25 million hectares and the planting of 184 million trees. He pointed out that the Kingdom's environmental sustainability efforts had extended to the regional level through the Middle East Green Initiative, which has attracted more than 35 countries. At the global level, he highlighted notable initiatives, including the launch of the Global Coral Reef Research and Development Accelerator Platform in 2020 during the G20 Summit and the Riyadh Global Drought Resilience Partnership at the 2024 Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification. Al-Mushaiti affirmed that these achievements had been made through the grace of God Almighty and the Saudi formula for success. He said this formula is based on the support of the wise leadership, the ambition of Saudi citizens equipped with knowledge, education, and a commitment to hard work, and integration among the public and private sectors and members of society. These factors strengthen the Kingdom's development journey, advance its ambitious national targets, and reinforce its leading position across various fields.

items.title: Minister Al-Saif: Investments in Saudi Arabia exceed SR1.3 trillion in 2025
items.title_zh: Al-Saif部长：2025年沙特阿拉伯的投资将超过1.3万亿里亚尔
items.summary: RIYADH — Minister of Investment Fahad Al-Saif said that investments in Saudi Arabia exceeded SR1.3 trillion during 2025, and expected this year’s total to remain within a similar range. Attending a panel discussion at the Budget 2027 Forum in Riyadh on Wednesday, the minister said investment rose by 6 percent in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025. Al-Saif affirmed that clear spending priorities bolster investor confidence, enabling the private sector to plan, expand, contribute to economic diversification, and create job opportunities for Saudi citizens. He noted that the past five years had seen more than SR6 trillion poured into infrastructure, adding that investment had increased markedly over the last six months. **media[2799878]** The minister described Saudi Arabia as a primary destination for investors, citing streamlined procedures across several sectors, including energy supply, transport and logistics, telecommunications and technology services, as well as promising sectors such as tourism, which is attracting substantial capital. The minister said coordination between the investment and tourism sectors had resulted in agreements worth SR7 billion with 19 local investors across six destinations. He added that the ministry was working to facilitate the journey of investors in the Kingdom, particularly local ones, who are capable of attracting foreign capital.He revealed that 76 deals worth SR95 billion were completed in 2026 across various sectors. The minister also noted that the Kingdom enjoys considerable diversity and competitive advantages across its regions, particularly in coastal areas, which offer attractive opportunities for investment in technology, tourism, and logistics, supported by an integrated telecommunications and digital ecosystem and a comprehensive transport network linking the entire country. Al-Saif said the coming period would see the activation of special economic zones, including the King Salman Automotive Cluster, where investment has exceeded SR80 billion. He stated that 90 percent of the SR6 trillion invested over the past five years came from domestic sources led by major Saudi companies, firms linked to capital markets, and small and medium-sized enterprises, which accounted for 30 percent of the total.

items.title: King Salman extends Citizen Account Program and additional support for a full year
items.title_zh: 萨勒曼国王将公民账户计划和额外补助延长至整整一年
items.summary: RIYADH — Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman has ordered the extension of the Citizen Account Program along with the provision of additional support to its beneficiaries for another full year. This decision was in line with the recommendation of Crown Prince, Prime Minister and Chairman of the Council of Economic and Development Affairs Mohammed bin Salman, the Saudi Press Agency reported on Wednesday. As per the royal order, the Citizen Account Program and additional support will continue to be provided to its beneficiaries through the end of the year 2027. This is in addition to continuing to open the registration for the program. The King’s directive comes out of the Saudi leadership’s utmost keenness and care for the Saudi citizens. Saudi Arabia launched the Citizen Account Program to protect Saudi families from the expected direct and indirect impact of various economic reforms, which may cause an additional burden on society, it was pointed out.

items.title: Aramco, S-OIL inaugurate Shaheen project in Korea
items.title_zh: 沙特阿美与S-OIL在韩国启动沙欣项目
items.summary: DHAHRAN — Saudi Aramco and its subsidiary S-OIL inaugurated the Shaheen Project at a ceremony held in Seoul, capital of the Republic of Korea, on Wednesday. The project is Aramco’s largest investment in the country, and the inauguration was attended by senior government and business leaders from Saudi Arabia and Korea, in addition to representatives of the energy and chemicals industries. It coincides with S-OIL’s 50th anniversary and represents an important milestone in the 35-year strategic partnership between Aramco and S-OIL, a relationship that began with Aramco’s initial S-OIL investment in 1991. Aramco President and CEO Amin H. Nasser said: “Economic headwinds and rising geopolitical risks do not alter our long-term view on strategic investments. One clear example is Shaheen, our largest ever investment in Korea, reflecting our confidence in the country and in the region that will drive future energy demand. Investments like Shaheen build the resilience that markets need in uncertain times. Through Aramco’s thermal crude to chemicals technology, deployed at scale, the project will strengthen S-OIL’s international competitiveness and create more value from every barrel. Together, we are positioned to meet the rising demand for materials essential to Asia’s key industries, from electric vehicles to semiconductors. As S-OIL celebrates its 50th anniversary, we are building the foundation for its next 50 years and beyond.” Aramco Downstream President Mohammed Y. Al Qahtani said: “Petrochemicals are critical to overall industrial competitiveness, and Shaheen brings cutting-edge technology to the region, helping position Korea as one of the world’s most competitive producers by prioritizing efficiency, technological differentiation, and value addition. Our investment in S-OIL and Shaheen underscores our long-term vision for this partnership, with a focus on advanced manufacturing that is expected to support product diversification and industrial growth and help meet rising demand for petrochemical feedstock in the years to come.” Representative Director and CEO of S-OIL Anwar A. Al-Hejazi said: “We are proud to celebrate this milestone with Aramco. We will continue to strengthen synergies across our refining, petrochemical, and lube base oil businesses and enhance our global competitiveness through continuous innovation and investment, leading S-OIL's growth into its next 50 years.” The $7 billion Shaheen project is a transformative step for both the Republic of Korea’s downstream sector and Aramco’s integrated downstream value chain. Combining world-class refining capabilities with the first major commercial deployment of Aramco’s proprietary thermal crude to chemicals (TC2CTM) technology, it features the world’s largest single steam cracker, a propylene fractionator, crude-to-chemicals conversion facilities, and polymer production units.Shaheen is expected to add approximately 3.2 million tons of annual petrochemical production capacity for S-OIL, positioning the company as a key player in the global supply of high-value polymers and advanced materials.By deploying Aramco’s TC2CTM technology, developed in collaboration with Lummus Technology, the project integrates refining and petrochemical processes to increase the share of crude oil converted into high-value chemicals. This expanded petrochemical production is projected to increase the share of petrochemicals in S-OIL’s overall business portfolio from 12 percent to 25 percent. The project will be integrated with S-OIL’s existing refining and petrochemical facilities in Ulsan, aiming to create synergies with other companies across the Ulsan petrochemical complex. Through dedicated pipeline networks, the facility is expected to provide a stable domestic supply of basic petrochemical feedstocks to nearby downstream companies, reducing their reliance on imports and logistics. This integration aims to strengthen the competitiveness of the broader petrochemical value chain and contribute to the development of Ulsan’s industrial ecosystem. Commercial operations are scheduled to commence in 2027 following the completion of commissioning. Aramco is the majority shareholder of S-OIL, holding more than 63 percent of the company’s shares on a non-diluted basis through its subsidiary Aramco Downstream Asia Pte. Ltd.

items.title: Saudi Arabia’s health coverage reaches 97%, delivering over 109 million services in 2026
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯的医疗保险覆盖率达到97%，2026年将提供超过1.09亿项服务
items.summary: RIYADH — Assistant Minister of Health for Health Services Dr. Mohammed Al-Abdulaali said that the health ecosystem in Saudi Arabia has delivered more than 109 million services in 2026 and added 116 projects, including 15 new ones and the development of over 101 sites. Health coverage of population clusters reached 97 percent, surgeries rose to 13,000 per week, and 94.6% of emergency patients received care within four hours, he said while addressing the Budget 2027 Forum in Riyadh on Wednesday. Abdulaali reviewed the health ecosystem's main achievements in 2026. He highlighted the progress in improving access to care and raising service quality under the Health Sector Transformation Program, part of Saudi Vision 2030. Al-Abdulaali noted that the beneficiary experience index rose to more than 89 percent, up from 66 percent in 2017, according to an independent international measurement. He added that the results motivate continued work to bring care closer, improve services, and put prevention first.

items.title: Alswaha: Saudi Arabia to launch smart assistant for every citizen in Q1 2027
items.title_zh: Alswaha：沙特阿拉伯将于2027年第一季度为每位公民推出智能助手
items.summary: RIYADH — Minister of Communications and Information Technology Abdullah Alswaha announced plans to launch a smart assistant for every citizen in the first quarter of 2027 through the Saudi Data and AI Authority. “It will let beneficiaries interact by voice in their local dialects, with government services such as passport renewal, vaccinations, and school registration. An initial trial with 500 users will expand to thousands before launch,” he said while speaking at the Budget 2027 Forum in Riyadh on Wednesday. **media[2799763]** Alswaha said Saudi Arabia is moving toward its goal of ranking among the world's top five countries in artificial intelligence (AI), building on its achievements in telecommunications and digital government, as its digital economy approaches half a trillion riyals. The minister indicated that digital trade between institutions and individuals grew 30 percent in the last quarter to reach SR100 billion, and praised the efforts of 420,000 Saudi men and women working in the sector. He noted that the Kingdom ranked fourth globally in the overall digital government index and first in five of its main indicators, including government services, surpassing the Saudi Vision 2030 target four years ahead of schedule. Alswaha said the Kingdom is shifting from digital to AI-based government. Government platforms were merged, reducing their number from 800 to 450, and more than 1,800 services are now available through the "Tawakkalna" app. He added that the Kingdom is working on three AI pillars: developing infrastructure and data centers, leading the adoption of AI applications, and enhancing the competitiveness of national talent and companies.
